text:
marta: Heads-up — discovered a provenance mismatch between the golden set and the latest holdout used for the quant4b experiments. small batch of anchors have duplicate fingerprints but different metadata. need quick decision on reconciliation strategy.

josh: ugh. do we know if it's a tokenizer change or ingestion double-ingest?

marta: initial diff shows identical text but different source_id and created_at. ingestion pipeline may have reingested from archival import v2.

anita: can you paste an example?

marta: sure — sample id: anchor-297b. fingerprints: sha1=6f5a3... and md5=c2b1... but source ids: s3://curation/seedbank/2024-11-01/anchor-297b.json vs s3://curation/legacy/anchor-297b.json

rui: that suggests provenance only, not content drift. for dedupe I’d prefer we collapse on content fingerprint and keep the canonical entry with latest qc_status and label history.

sam: +1 to collapse by content fingerprint but preserve provenance chain as an ordered list field (so we don't lose which dataset introduced the anchor). Also need to mark any anchors used by quant experiments for potential regression tracing.

marta: operationally, that means: 1) run content-fingerprint dedupe (sha1) with keep_policy=latest_qc 2) merge provenance arrays 3) emit migration mapping for rollbacks. ok?

josh: we should add an exception for anchors with conflicting golden labels. if label_history differs (golden vs relabel) don't auto-merge — flag for manual review by @labeling-team.

anita: agree. we saw a case where two identical prompts had different golden answers because of a format-normalization change. manual review required.

labeler_bot: deploy scheduled: provenance-reconcile-job v1.3 queued on prod-curation at 1758884300. ETA ~20m. logs will be in http://logs.redwood.internal/provenance/1758884300

marta: thanks bot. adding one more constraint: anchors with usage_count>100 in production routes should not be removed during the first pass; just annotate and queue for phased rollback to avoid impacting eval baselines.

rui: for the quant team — any anchors that were part of the quant4b dev holdout, tag them with quant.experiment=quant4b-2025-01 and snapshot their embeddings. we need to rerun a small regression test if any provenance merges touch them.

sam: note on embeddings: we should store both pre-quant and post-quant embeddings if available, naming convention: anchor-<id>--embed-prequant/<id>.npy and anchor-<id>--embed-quant4b/<id>.npy in s3. makes rollback comparisons easier.

josh: small snippet for the dedupe job config I pushed to infra repo:
```json
{"fingerprint_algo":"sha1","keep_policy":"latest_qc","manual_review_tag":"golden_conflict","preserve_provenance":true}
```

anita: will the job also emit a CSV map for labelers to review? we need a human-readable report for the manual review queue.

marta: yes — the job emits: reconciliation_report.csv (cols: anchor_id, kept_id, conflicting_labels, provenance_list, usage_count, suggested_action). I'll add sampling slices for labeler throughput planning.

labeler_bot: manual review queue created: qid=prov-review-1758884500. labelers notified: @labeling-team.

sam: timeline expectation? if the job runs now and manual review is ~1k anchors, we should expect ~48h to finish with current capacity. any way to triage automatically?

josh: we can auto-approve if conflicting_labels are identical after punctuation normalization and whitespace collapse. only escalate if semantic differences remain.

anita: add normalization step to pipeline: lowercase + unicode normalize + collapse whitespace + strip punctuation edges. that will reduce manual hits.

marta: ok I'll update the job config and kick it off after QA. final checklist: update dedupe job config in infra, notify quant to snapshot embeddings, set keep_policy exceptions for high-usage anchors, generate CSV and tag manual review. I'm going to run a dry-run now and post logs.

rui: thanks — ping here when dry-run logs are up and we'll sanity-check sample of merged entries for eval stability. :eyes:
